summary: A list of the people and organisations who care about a project, programme or operation, and how much say each has in it.
example: Quality Check Rollout stakeholders: the analytics partner cares a lot and has some say; the transport contractor has little of either.
definition: The people and organisations who affect or are affected by one project, programme or operation, and how much say each has. Each entry is a resource or one of the work's beneficiary groups. You first mark each as primary (directly affected) or secondary (indirectly affected), then place them by influence and interest, which sets how to work with them: manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, or monitor. It is not the list of roles the work needs, and not a list of named people.

/spec/scope.guide: The project, programme or operation this map is about. Add it first if it does not exist.

poor.why: A team cannot have a stakeholder map. Choose the project, programme or operation the team runs.

/metadata/name.guide: The name of the project, programme or operation followed by "stakeholders".

poor.why: Too general. Add the name of the project, programme or operation.

/spec/entries.guide: One entry for each stakeholder, chosen from your resources or the work's beneficiary groups. A stakeholder does not have to be part of the work. You can add one now and place it on the grid later.

/spec/entries/-/group.guide: A beneficiary group of the work, when the stakeholder is the people it helps. Choose a group the work already names. Choose a group or a resource, not both.

poor.text: delivering-members, also added as a Resource
poor.why: The same people added twice. Choose the group only.

/spec/entries/-/resource.guide: The stakeholder, chosen from your resources: a role, unit, partner, system or place, inside or outside your organisation. Add it as a resource first if it is missing. For the people the work helps, choose a beneficiary group instead.

poor.why: A person. Choose the role or organisation instead.
Too broad. Choose a unit or role from your resources.

/spec/entries/-/stake.guide: What this stakeholder cares about in this work, in one sentence.
good: Wants fewer rejected loads, and no slower intake at busy depots.
Must sign off any change to how member delivery records are kept.

poor.why: Says who they are, not what they care about.
Says how much, not what they care about.

/spec/entries/-/owner.guide: The role that manages the relationship with this stakeholder, chosen from your resources. Not a person.

poor.why: A person. Choose their role instead.

/spec/entries/-/tier.guide: Primary if the work affects them directly, secondary if indirectly. A secondary stakeholder can still have a lot of influence.

/spec/entries/-/influence.guide: How much this stakeholder can change what happens, from 1 (little) to 3 (a great deal). Leave it empty until you have assessed it.

/spec/entries/-/interest.guide: How much this stakeholder cares what happens, from 1 (little) to 3 (a great deal). Leave it blank until it is assessed.

checks.stakeholders-identified: Add everyone the work affects and everyone who can affect it.
checks.stakeholders-placed: Give each stakeholder an influence and an interest score from 1 to 3.
